brand_ilford.note: Two companies print ILFORD on a box. Harman Technology trades as Ilford Photo under licence for the black and white range; Ilford Imaging Europe GmbH owns the trademark and sells the Ilfocolor colour films. Neither is a parent of the other, so no parentBrandId edge exists between Ilford and Harman.

brand_kentmere.note: parentBrandId = Harman. Genuine ownership: Harman acquired Kentmere Photographic in 2007 and moved production to Mobberley.

brand_yesstar.note: Corporate entity is Yestar Healthcare Holdings, operating in Nanning via Guangxi Giant Star Medical Equipment Co Ltd. Both carried as aliases so the spelling mismatch resolves on search.

Fujifilm 400.note: Superia X-tra 400 was discontinued in all markets in 2024 and replaced by Fujifilm 400, contract manufactured by Kodak and made in the USA. Distinct from Fujicolor 400, which is a separate regional product — the pair is the reason the two rows must not be merged.

Lomography Color Negative 400.note: Long-standing community consensus, never officially confirmed. Lomography coats no film of its own.

Yes!Star 400.note: Two layers of rebrand. Fujifilm moved C200/C400 production to China in 2024 with Yes!Star as production partner, and Yes!Star 400 is reported to be rebranded Fujifilm C400; separately the facility is described as a finishing operation cutting and packaging Kodak master rolls rather than coating emulsion. Fujifilm C400 is not a row in this catalogue — do not invent it. Research item for phase 3's parentStockId.

Ilford HP5 Plus 400.note: Harman Technology, trading as Ilford Photo, Mobberley UK.

Kentmere Pan 400.note: Kentmere is the brand, Harman coats it. This is the distinction the single manufacturer column destroyed.

Cinestill 800T.note: Kodak Vision3 500T with the remjet removed. The stock relationship itself belongs to phase 3 parentStockId; Vision3 500T is already a row here.

Lucky Color 200.note: China Lucky Film's own coating in Baoding, Hebei. Launched at the Shanghai Image & Vision Expo in July 2025, the company's first colour film since discontinuing its range in 2012, initial run around 10,000 rolls. Not a respool — the earlier assumption that it was came from Lucky's history as a Kodak OEM partner.

Lucky Color 400.note: Followed Lucky Color 200 within roughly half a year. Same coating operation.

Orwo Wolfen NC400.note: ORWO, still coating at the original Bitterfeld-Wolfen site. Colour balance is daylight per retailer listings — filled from a source, having deliberately been left null rather than inferred from the other twenty C-41 rows. Carries no remjet and runs in either C-41 or ECN-2; recorded as C-41, which is how it is sold for still photography. First case arguing for `process` becoming a set rather than a scalar.

Ilford IlfoColor 400 Plus.note: Ilfocolor 400 Plus Vintage Tone. 24 exposures, muted warm tones, selective saturation, lower contrast. A distinct product from Ilfocolor Vivid 400, not a casing variant of it — merging the two would have destroyed a real stock. Coater undisclosed; one well-sourced analysis suggests ORWO. A historical Ilfocolor 400 Plus sold in Italy around 2005 was made by Ferrania and must not be conflated with this.

Ilford Ilfocolor Vivid 400.note: 36 exposures, saturated and punchy, compared by reviewers to Ektar. Distinct product from Vintage Tone. Coater undisclosed.

Fujicolor 400.note: Separate regional product from Fujifilm 400. Fuji's consumer 400 offerings are regionalised and the US product is not the same as elsewhere. Origin unconfirmed.

Fujifilm Superia Premium 400.note: NOT RESEARCHED. A Japan-market product with its own history. UNKNOWN here records that nobody has checked, which is deliberately not the same claim as in-house. Needs its own sourcing before a status is set.

LomoChrome Color '92 Sun-Kissed.note: Lomography claims its own formula; the coater is undisclosed.
